statements.markdown:
A nonempty support with a terminal complementary component has a last
point $r<1$. Its plateau
has positive height, since a neighbourhood of $r$ has positive measure.
The contact values and slope at $r$, including the one-sided case $r=0$,
and positive-plateau curvature meet the calculus hypotheses. Since
$0\le q\le1$, integration gives $G(r)<0$, contradicting atom addition.
This is an ordinary consequence of the previously stated inputs. The
quantitative proof above is retained for its stronger estimate (5.1).

statements.markdown:
**Theorem 1 (full support; quantitative proof following
[OpenAI (2026a), Theorem 1.1][FS]).**
If $\gamma\in\mathcal U$ minimises $\mathcal P$, then
$$
\operatorname{supp}\mu_\gamma=[0,1),\qquad
\gamma(t_2)>\gamma(t_1)\quad(0\leq t_1<t_2<1).
$$
For the solution of the displayed SDE and every $0\leq t<1$,
$$
q(t)=t,\qquad \mathbb E[a(t,X_t)^2]=1.
$$

statements.markdown:
**Source theorem ([OpenAI (2026a), Theorem 1.1][support-manuscript]).**
In the pure, zero-field model with $\xi(t)=t^2/2$, let $\gamma$ be an
admissible integrable minimiser of $\mathcal P$. Its Stieltjes measure
has full relative support on $[0,1)$, and $\gamma$ is strictly increasing.
For every associated diffusion and every $0\le t<1$,

$$
\mathbb E[u(t,X_t)^2]=t,\qquad
\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)^2]=1.
$$
